# STUR Physics Lab: one simulation. Information for AI and LLM readers.

> The repository holds one script, production_v2_2.py: Python 3.8+, standard library
> only, with nothing tuned and nothing fitted. Measured inputs (PDG 2024, Planck 2018,
> CODATA, SI) are in INPUTS. Measured results used only for judging are in COMPARISONS.
> Numerical settings are in NUMERICS. Everything else is calculated. A test fails if a
> non-integer number appears outside those tables.

## What it computes
- Cosmology (flat LambdaCDM): Omega_r from T_CMB and N_eff, Omega_Lambda from flatness,
  age 13.795 Gyr (Planck: 13.787 +/- 0.020), q0, z_acc = 0.631, z_eq, horizon entropies.
- Quark flavour: quark masses run with the RG (two-loop QCD, one-loop QED, one-loop SM
  Yukawa/gauge above m_t) to 1.5-10 TeV, put into the Fritzsch six-zero texture, and
  diagonalized exactly. The two free phases are scanned over [0, 2pi).
- Result: |V_us|, |V_ub| and J are inside their bands. |V_cb| (32 sigma), |V_ub/V_cb|
  (14 sigma) and |V_td/V_ts| (5 sigma) are outside for every phase, so the six-zero
  texture is excluded.

- Texture survey: all 1,000 pairs of Hermitian quark mass matrices with 5 or 6 zeros
  (188 classes). 83 make predictions; 82 are excluded, and one survives (up 00X/0XX/XXX,
  down Fritzsch 0X0/X0X/0XX; chi^2 = 0.3 for 1 dof). No unknown is fixed: the band test is
  exact, and the joint test only decides survival.
- 3-3-1 (beta = +-1/sqrt3): every mass-matrix entry is gauge-allowed, so 3-3-1 forces no
  texture zero. The triplet family makes the survivor three distinct 3-3-1 hypotheses.

- Flavour symmetry (Part E): with the minimal 3-3-1 scalars, no abelian Z_N (N <= 6, exhaustive)
  makes a texture zero that keeps three-family mixing. Hermitian matrices cannot come from a
  symmetry commuting with SU(3)_L. Z_6 with 6 scalar triplets gives the survivor's zeros, but as
  general matrices they have 14 parameters for 10 observables (-4 predictions). Conclusion: no
  flavour symmetry inside 3-3-1 makes the survivor predictive.

- Closure (Part F): all 61,009 zero-pattern pairs of general quark mass matrices (497 classes).
  Ranks proved (exact lower bound at integer points meets a symmetry upper bound), J = 0 proved
  by symbolic expansion: every pattern with three-family mixing and
  CP violation has exactly 10 physical parameters, so none predicts anything. Inside 3-3-1 the
  quark sector closes with 10 measured inputs (6 masses, 4 CKM parameters).
- Part G: the same in the Standard Model (general zeros, Part F) and in left-right models
  (parallel Hermitian textures; all 3 predictive ones excluded at >= 31 sigma). Texture zeros
  calculate no CKM number in any of the three frameworks.

- Part H (quantum and gravity, established physics): Planck units; the one-loop correction to
  Newton's law (41/(10 pi), quoted); Hawking, de Sitter and Unruh temperatures; gravity-mediated
  entanglement (smallest mass gravity can ever entangle maximally: (pi hbar^2/(G c t0))^(1/3) =
  89 MeV, same combination as Weinberg's pion relation; zero if gravity is classical); the
  proton/Planck hierarchy from logarithmic running. Exact identities: alpha_G = (m_p/M_P)^2,
  S_dS * rho_Lambda/rho_P = 3/8.

- Part I (alpha): grand unification at two loops from alpha_s and sin^2 theta_W. SM cannot
  unify (needs 1/alpha = 81.8 vs 127.95). In the MSSM, alpha is a function of the unknown
  superpartner scale; the measured value points to M_S ~ 2.5 TeV. Closed formulas for 1/alpha
  (Eddington, Wyler, 4pi^3+pi^2+pi) are excluded by >= 4000 sigma.

- Part J (Yukawas): SU(5) m_s/m_d = m_mu/m_e off by 558 sigma; Georgi-Jarlskog off by 10 sigma.
  b-tau unification fails in the SM (0.59-0.70); in the MSSM (scales from Part I) it needs
  tan(beta) = 1.33, and the top quasi-fixed point needs 1.31-1.38. No Yukawa is calculated.
- Part K (Higgs mass, MSSM): with Part I's M_S and Part J's tan(beta), maximal stop mixing gives m_h <= 102.9 GeV vs measured 125.20; that MSSM route is excluded.
- Part L (SM criticality): lambda(M_P) = 0, two-loop running, one-loop matching to pole masses, predicts M_h = 129.0 +/- 0.9 GeV vs 125.20 (matching shifts it +0.04 GeV); with lambda = beta_lambda = 0, M_t = 173.5 GeV. Measured M_h gives lambda(M_P) = -0.012.
- Part N (masses): Koide's Q = 2/3 fits the charged-lepton pole masses (0.4 sigma) but fails at M_Z (225 sigma) and for quarks (>= 99 sigma). No mass is calculated.
- Part O (strong CP): chiral log gives d_n = 2.05e-16 theta-bar e cm, so |theta-bar| < 8.8e-11 (2.2e-10 weakest). m_u = 0 excluded (31 sigma); axion: m_a = 5.77 micro-eV x 1e12 GeV/f_a (a trade); parity gives arg det in {0, pi} but needs excluded textures.
- Part P (neutrinos): smallest sum 58.8 meV (NO), 98.9 meV (IO, excluded at 95% by DESI DR2 + CMB); m_bb bands with Majorana phases scanned; fixed mixing patterns excluded by theta13 (39 sigma); TM1 survives and predicts delta ~ 262 deg; seesaw scale <= 7.6e15 GeV, so Part L's SM-to-M_P needs Dirac neutrinos.
- Part Q (proton decay): dimension-6 p -> e+ pi0 at Part I's M_GUT and alpha_GUT gives 2.4e35 yr, 10x the Super-K limit 2.4e34; the SM's g1 = g2 point gives 5e23 yr (excluded). Dimension-5 p -> nubar K+ in minimal SUSY SU(5) (M_HC = M_GUT, superpartners at M_S, tan beta 1.3) gives 3e28-7e29 yr vs 5.9e33: excluded.
- Part R (anomalies, exact): anomaly cancellation + Yukawas give the SM hypercharges uniquely and quantize charge (q_p + q_e = 0); nu_R opens B - L (neutron charge eps), a Majorana mass closes it; 3-3-1 needs N_families a multiple of 3 and QCD asymptotic freedom leaves exactly 3.
- Part S (baryon asymmetry): eta_B = 6.12e-10 from Omega_b h^2 and T_CMB. SM fails: crossover (m_h 31 sigma above the lattice endpoint 72.4 GeV), CP measure 4e-24. Leptogenesis: sphaleron 28/79 and g* derived; efficiency kappa_f calculated (z_B solved); needs M_1 >= 6.5e8 GeV at full efficiency, 1.5e10-1.3e11 GeV in the natural washout range.
- Part T (SO(10)): B - L needs nu^c; sin^2 theta_W = 3/8 and the 3/5 normalization derived; minimal 10_H Yukawas excluded; t-b-tau needs a ~+28% m_b threshold; non-SUSY SO(10) via Pati-Salam unifies at one loop with M_I = 5.5e11, M_GUT = 1.1e16 GeV, passes proton decay, and puts the seesaw scale where leptogenesis needs it.
- Part T5 (SO(10) chains, two loops): PS M_I = 1.4e11, M_GUT = 8.0e15; PS+D and LR+D excluded by proton decay; LR M_I = 2.8e9.
- Part T6 (vacuum): lambda(M_I) = 0 is not required (tree threshold lambda_H - lambda_HS^2/lambda_S); stability needs M_I below mu_0 = 6.2e10 GeV: LR chains yes, PS undecided by M_t, PS+D no.
- Part T7 (thresholds +-1 in 1/alpha): only PS+D's proton-decay exclusion is robust; LR+D's exclusion and PS/LR verdicts depend on the heavy spectrum.
- Part T8 (heavy spectrum): Pati-Salam's heavy GUT multiplets by group theory; the SU(2)_L triplets (10,3,1) of 126 and (15,3,1) of 210 dominate; within a factor 10 of M_GUT, tau_p spans 1e27-1e43 yr: the spectrum decides.
- Part T9 (210 potential): every invariant of the 210, vev on the PS singlet, Goldstones massless (check); over the viable coupling box ~80% of potentials pass proton decay, median tau_p ~1e35 yr, M_I ~1.5e11 GeV; Part T10: the 126 from its couplings to <210>: m^2(10,3,1) = 2 eta_2 v exactly; with both scanned, most viable potentials pass proton decay and natural leptogenesis. Part T11: the 10's one splitting quartic H_i H_j phi_iklm phi_jklm and its mixing with the 126's (6,1,1); light doublet assumed (doublet-triplet tuning); the colour triplet sits near M_GUT.
- Part V (axion dark matter): misalignment from its ingredients reproduces Di Luzio et al.'s eq. 170; all the DM post-inflation at f_a = 2.0e11 GeV (m_a = 28.5 micro-eV); at Pati-Salam's M_I the axion gives 65% of the DM, at the left-right M_I under 1%.
- Part W (W mass): SM two-loop M_W (Awramik et al. parametrization) = 80.350 +/- 0.004 GeV at Part L's m_h; PDG fit 80.353, measured 80.360 (no CDF) / 80.369: within 1.4 sigma.
- Part X (closed cosmology): Omega_m from Omega_b + the axion at PS's M_I (misalignment) + neutrinos gives age 15.2 Gyr, 70 sigma off Planck; strings/defects must supply ~35% of the dark matter. Part W also gives sin^2 theta_eff = 0.23164 vs 0.23151 (LEP+SLC).
- Part Y (SO(10) Yukawas): exact selection rule: in the PS chain the light Higgs is in one SU(4) irrep, M_e = M_d or -3 M_d: excluded (m_mu/m_s = 3.8, m_e/m_d = 0.36 at M_I). In the LR chain the 10+126 sum rule M_e = c1 M_d + c2 M_u reaches the lepton masses (8 unknowns: neutrinos next). The survivor moves from PS to LR.
- One running (item 6): every mass and mixing above m_t(m_t) from one engine (gauge + full 3x3 Yukawa matrices, all generations and CKM; SM, MSSM above M_S with tan(beta) matching, LR above M_I). MSSM matrix RGE checked against the general superpotential formula (1e-16); Part J's third-generation running is the engine on that subspace; the light generations move it by 0.03-0.04 %.
- Part Y running: between M_I and M_GUT the LR theory's own one-loop matrix RGE (derived from the general Machacek-Vaughn formula over every component, checked to 1e-16); u_R, d_R share an SU(2)_R doublet, so y_t pushes y_b up. (m_b - m_tau)/m_b at M_GUT: -0.60 (SM running) -> -0.41 (LR running).
- Part Y3 (type-II neutrinos from the sum rule): excluded at ~19 sigma; b and tau still do not converge.
- Part Y4 (type I and I + II): type I adds no unknown; types I + II: 11 fits (best chi^2 0.0 for 13 data, 17 unknowns), delta 36-353 deg (not pinned; fit count and range are search-dependent). The neutrino tension, settled: the perturbative bound is M_R,3 <= 2 sqrt(4 pi) M_I/g_R ~ 12.6 M_I; in SO(10) the Delta_R coupling is Y126 = (M_d - M_e)/4d, and the fits fix |b/d| ~ 30 (|a/c| ~ 60), so |d| = k sqrt(f/(1+|b/d|^2)) and v_R ~ 4e12-2e13 GeV, 800-4000 times the chain's; perturbativity alone keeps v_R >= 14 times the chain's (inside the x31 threshold band); with T13's 126 share it is >= 800x: the chain fails the neutrinos, by a margin 30x smaller than before.
- 5b: a real 10 forces |c2| = |1 - c1| (self-conjugate bidoublet) and then misses the charged leptons (chi^2 6e3): the 10 must be complex. The complex 10's own potential (T13): the light complex bidoublet fixes D10 = X X^T/m_126; 4073 of 8648 draws viable; the fits' |a/c|, |b/d| pin the light Higgs's direction (two circles), so each point predicts d: 52 points match, every one with v_R >= 3600 x its chain's.
- 5c: MS-bar heavy-vector matching constants T_i/12pi at M_I and M_GUT (no unknown; M_I +5 %, M_GUT +4 %); second bidoublet vev |k2/k1| <= m_b/m_t moves (m_b - m_tau)/m_b to -0.48..-0.35; the Delta_R coupling (RGE derived, checked to 1e-16) only makes tau heavier (-1.58 at the perturbative maximum).
- 7: full 3-3-1 anomaly set with lepton triplets and U(1)_X cancels exactly for beta = +-1/sqrt3 (fails without the leptons); the dimension-five factor vs Hisano eq. 19 is 1.65 (newer alpha_p) x 1.37 (eq. 19's rounding and 2013 inputs): not a bug; the scaling is exact.
- Part AA (item 8): all 28 multiplets of the minimal LR theory are R-even under (-1)^(3(B-L)+2s): no dark-matter candidate besides the axion (0.7 %). Inflation from slow roll: phi^4 (r 0.26-0.31) and phi^2 (r 0.13-0.16) excluded, the xi phi^2 R plateau (n_s 0.962-0.968, r 0.003-0.004) allowed; SM Higgs inflation excluded (lambda < 0 above mu_0 = 6e10 GeV would need lambda ~ 1e21).
- Part Z (ledger): every free number of SM + cosmology has a computed status for each closest hypothesis (LR, PS, LR+D: one fail each, ties carried); for LR: calculated 2 (charges, sin^2 theta_W = 3/8), input 4 (vev, quark masses, CKM, G), traded 3, bounded 1, open 5. The family number (3-3-1 only) and the Hermitian CKM texture are not credited: neither belongs to the closest hypothesis. No continuous SM parameter is calculated.
- Part U (scorecard): labels by fixed rules (pass = a test that could fail; trade = an unknown absorbs it; open = no mechanism or not imposed, e.g. lambda(M_I) = 0). SM to M_P fails unification, b-tau, Higgs (3.3 sigma), baryon asymmetry; minimal SUSY SU(5) fails the Higgs mass, proton decay and fermion masses; SO(10) via Pati-Salam fails the fermion masses (Part Y), via left-right the neutrinos (Part Y4), LR+D proton decay (threshold-sensitive), PS+D proton decay and fermion masses: no complete hypothesis survives; each SO(10) chain passes at most one real test (proton decay).
- Lineage: every stage carries its field content; results handed between different field contents are listed with a reason (a test fails if one has none).
- Every scale comes from the algorithm: m_t(m_t), Part I's M_S = 2.54 TeV and M_GUT, M_Planck.

## Files
- production_v2_2.py: the simulation
- results/production_v2_2.txt: expected output
- tests/test_production.py: the no-tuning rule and the pinned numbers
- archive/: notes and the 3-3-1 paper from the earlier codebase
